## Purpose and Entry Points
Taskflow is a header-only C++20 library for CPU task-graph parallelism and optional CUDA Graph execution. Consumer programs include the umbrella header `taskflow/taskflow.hpp`, construct `tf::Taskflow` graphs, and submit them to `tf::Executor`. C++ modules provide an alternative import surface in `modules/tf.cppm` and `modules/tf_with_cuda.cppm`.

## Graph Construction Model
`tf::Taskflow` owns a dependency graph; `tf::FlowBuilder` supplies task creation, dependencies, composition, and algorithm-building APIs. Task nodes represent static work, conditions, modules, subflows, and runtime-generated work; edges govern readiness and control-flow choices.
- `taskflow/core/taskflow.hpp`
- `taskflow/core/flow_builder.hpp`
- `taskflow/core/graph.hpp`
- `taskflow/core/task.hpp`

## CPU Execution Runtime
`tf::Executor` is the primary control boundary between a user-defined graph and concurrent execution. It owns worker threads, submits graph runs as topologies, tracks completion through futures, and supports cancellation, observer hooks, and thread-safe asynchronous submissions. Scheduling is work-stealing based, using per-worker queues and notification primitives rather than an external runtime service.
- `taskflow/core/executor.hpp`
- `taskflow/core/topology.hpp`
- `taskflow/core/worker.hpp`
- `taskflow/core/wsq.hpp`

## Dynamic and Asynchronous Tasking
Graph execution can expand dynamically: subflow tasks receive a `tf::Subflow` to build child graphs, while runtime tasks can create work during execution. Separately, executor-level async and dependent-async APIs submit tasks outside a persistent `Taskflow` graph, returning futures or dependency handles. These paths converge on the same executor/worker scheduling domain.
- `taskflow/core/async.hpp`
- `taskflow/core/async_task.hpp`
- `taskflow/core/runtime.hpp`
- `taskflow/core/task_group.hpp`

## Parallel Algorithms and Pipelines
High-level algorithms compile user ranges and operations into graph tasks, using partitioner policies to divide work. Pipeline abstractions represent tokenized, staged execution and can be composed into a taskflow; data pipelines add typed inter-stage data movement. This layer is built over core graph/executor primitives, not a separate processing engine.
- `taskflow/algorithm/algorithm.hpp`
- `taskflow/algorithm/partitioner.hpp`
- `taskflow/algorithm/pipeline.hpp`
- `taskflow/algorithm/data_pipeline.hpp`

## CUDA Boundary
CUDA support is optional and isolated under `taskflow/cuda`. CPU tasks can construct CUDA graphs containing memory transfers and kernels, instantiate executable graphs, and launch them on CUDA streams. CUDA algorithm wrappers and execution policies expose GPU parallel operations; NVIDIA CUDA Toolkit/nvcc is the material external dependency, with cuBLAS discovery support in `cmake/cuda/modules/FindcuBLAS.cmake`.
- `taskflow/cuda/cudaflow.hpp`
- `taskflow/cuda/cuda_graph.hpp`
- `taskflow/cuda/cuda_stream.hpp`
- `taskflow/cuda/algorithm/matmul.hpp`

## Observability, Packaging, and Validation
Observers instrument executor activity, including Chrome-trace output and TFProf records; the static TFProf viewer is shipped in `tfprof/`. CMake supports consumption and builds examples, benchmarks, and tests across Linux, macOS, and Windows. Bundled dependencies include CLI11, doctest, Eigen, FastFlow, TBB, and spdlog, mainly for development, comparison benchmarks, or optional examples rather than the core header runtime.
- `taskflow/observer/interface.hpp`
- `taskflow/observer/chrome.hpp`
- `taskflow/observer/tfprof.hpp`
- `CMakeLists.txt`
